results.title: Not in a mould | Anant Nag - The Hindu
results.article:
Veteran actor **Anant Nag**, known for his "behavioural" acting style, will receive the 2024 Dadasaheb Phalke Award at the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony in Gujarat on September 22. The award recognizes his five-decade contribution to Indian cinema across various genres. Nag previously won the Padma Bhushan last year and is the second Kannada actor to win the Phalke Award after Dr. Rajkumar.
“I would call it behaving, not acting,” veteran actor Anant Nag once said, pithily summing up his approach to the craft. With his skills forged on the Mumbai stage and not in a film school, reliance on what he called “behavioural” acting has stood Nag in good stead as he has easily moved between parallel and commercial cinema, exploring multiple genres from social drama to romance to comedy to horror. The actor will, on September 22, receive the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024, for his contribution to Indian cinema over five decades, at the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony in Gujarat. He was awarded Padma Bhushan last year. Nag is the second Kannada actor to win the Phalke after Dr. Rajkumar. Published - September 20, 2026 01:20 am IST

results.title: MSF warns $28,000 annual cost limits access to Gilead's HIV prevention injection
results.article: **Gilead Sciences** developed lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injection for HIV prevention. In 2024, a trial involving over 2,000 women in **South Africa** and **Uganda** showed zero infections. While the **FDA** approved it in June 2025, **MSF** warns that costs of $28,000 annually limit access. **UNAIDS** reported funding fell to $7.3bn in 2025. **Gilead** plans providing for 3 million people through 2028.

old.why_in_news: The FDA approval of lenacapavir, a breakthrough HIV prevention drug, highlights the tension between medical innovation and global healthcare equity.

results.title: Vijay launches ‘Vettri Payanam’ offering no-fare travel for 84.32 lakh women and transgender persons
results.article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, **Tamil Nadu** Chief Minister, launched the ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme on October 2, 2026, at **Koyambedu** bus terminus in **Chennai**. The expansion provides no-fare travel for women and transgender persons across 12,695 buses from seven **State Transport Corporations**, benefiting 84.32 lakh people daily. It excludes **Chengalpattu** and **Tiruppur** due to bypolls. **Vijay** announced the scheme on August 24.

results.title: IFSCA Executive Director: Companies will be automatically onboarded as listed entities
results.article: **Pradeep Ramakrishnan**, **IFSCA** Executive Director, announced at the **Morningstar Investment Conference India 2026** that companies will be automatically onboarded as listed entities. **GIFT IFSC** has raised nearly $85 billion in bonds and handles almost 75% of external commercial borrowings. The centre hosts 1,400 entities, including 235 fund management entities, while facilitating gold imports of 110 tonnes and silver of 1,200 tonnes.

results.title: Supreme Court Rejects Plea to Halt 0.4% UPI Charge on Big Transactions
results.article: On September 28, 2026, the **Supreme Court** refused a plea by petitioner Anjan Datta for an interim stay on the government's decision to levy a 0.4% charge on UPI person-to-merchant transactions over ₹2,000 from October 15, 2026. The court directed the **Union of India**, **Reserve Bank of India**, and **NPCI** to file counter affidavits within four weeks, questioning the legality of these charges as they might trigger cash transactions and black money issues.

old.why_in_news: The Supreme Court questioned the legal status of the 0.4% UPI merchant discount rate (MDR) as a potential 'expropriation' and its impact on the formal economy.
old.fact_box: The government proposed a 0.4% charge on UPI person-to-merchant transactions exceeding ₹2,000 starting October 15, 2026. The Supreme Court has sought counter affidavits from the Union of India, RBI, and NPCI regarding the legality and economic impact of this levy.

prelims_pointers.text: NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) is the primary body for operating the UPI infrastructure.
The proposed UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) is 0.4% for transactions above ₹2,000.
RBI (Reserve Bank of India) is the regulatory authority for the Indian payment systems.
